content.text: First CMC OA is common in older adults. CMC 1 OA can be quite disabling due to the importance of the thumb in most functional activities.
The thumb accounts for 40-50% of hand function, and the hand accounts for 90% of upper limb function.

With degeneration, the joint space narrows, leading to relative instability of the first CMC (which is highly mobile to begin with) and pain. Pain is normally felt around the anatomical snuffbox and/or thenar eminence, especially with thumb movement.
CMC 1 OA can lead to injury to the UCL of MCP 1 through a chain of compensations: thenar contracture → reduced thumb extension → compensatory excessive abduction → valgus stress at MCP 1.
Pain with movement felt mainly in the region of the snuffbox. Pain is worse in the morning but improves with some movement and the use of heat.

items: Gripping
Pinching
Radial deviation

content.text: Pain leads to disuse and then loss of function. Elderly may even avoid eating due to pain. It is common for people with CMC 1 OA to have OA in multiple joints or both hands.
Acutely swollen, red, taut, and warm joints are NOT expected with OA — these signs suggest RA instead.

content.title: Cautions
content.text: Do not mobilise CMC or take thumb to full ROM if osteophytes are present or abnormal bone to bone end feel occurs. Avoid joint compression and be careful with POP.

Ultimately, OA is a chronic, progressive condition. However, improvements in pain and hand function may be achieved in 4-12 weeks. The longer the condition has been present, the longer it will take for initial improvements.

Weekly treatment for 6 weeks should be an initial treatment plan, with treatment thereafter more spaced out, as long as the person is able to follow a home care plan of pain-free movement and intrinsic hand muscle strengthening.

quiz.question: If thumb pain is recreated during radial deviation of the wrist, what is the most likely condition?
quiz.explanation: CMC 1 OA is the most likely condition present if thumb pain is recreated during radial deviation of the wrist, because radial deviation is a compressive force on the CMC 1.

quiz.question: Which sign would suggest RA rather than OA in a patient with thumb joint pain?
options: Acutely swollen, red, taut, and warm joint
quiz.explanation: Acutely swollen, red, taut, and warm joints are not expected with OA — they suggest RA instead.

quiz.question: Joint mobilisation of the CMC is safe to perform even when osteophytes are present.
quiz.explanation: Do not mobilise CMC or take thumb to full ROM if osteophytes are present or abnormal bone-to-bone end feel occurs.
